title: Ang 719–720: Bairari
hookLine: a raga that fits on two pages
tomorrow: what did Guru Nanak say when an invading army came through?

cards: At a wedding the gift table fills up: big boxes, gold sets, envelopes thick with cash. Then someone sets down a small handwritten card and suddenly feels shy about it.
Bairari, a raga in the Guru Granth Sahib, fits on two pages, ang 719 and 720. So here's today's question: does small mean less?

teach.b: Bairari holds hymns by Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan, and one of them carries a whole teaching.

In paraphrase, ang 719: the Lord's servant sings the Name; if someone slanders that servant, the servant doesn't lose their own goodness. That's it. You don't hand over your goodness because someone takes a swing at you.
Another opens, in paraphrase: listen, mind, to the story of the Name that can't be told. The Granth doesn't rank a raga by its length.
These two pages are bound in the same book, and honored the same way, as the long ones. Christians have a picture of small things too.
In the King James Bible, Jesus says: "The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed," and Matthew adds, "Which indeed is the least of all seeds."
Here's what's shared: the smallest thing isn't the least important thing. And here's an honest difference.

teach.h: THE SEED GROWS; BAIRARI IS WHOLE.
teach.b: In Matthew the seed grows, into a tree where the birds come and lodge. Bairari doesn't grow. It stays two pages, and it's already whole.

how: Bairari's hymns are part of the Guru Granth Sahib like every other raga, read in full during a complete reading of the Granth and sung in kirtan.

games.q: you're asked to speak at your grandfather's birthday. your cousin has a long speech ready. you have two honest lines. what fits Bairari?
o: skip it; two lines will look like you didn't care.
say the two lines; a short thing can be whole.
pad it out so it's as long as your cousin's.
games.why: the Granth doesn't rank a raga by its length. Bairari is two pages and holds a whole teaching. small isn't less.

practice: Find the smallest thing within reach: a grain of rice, a seed, a button, a crumb. Rest it on your palm or the table in front of you, and look at it for the sit as if it were the only thing in the room.
Notice that it's already complete. Afterward, Bairari is short enough to read all of it.
